start.text: Hi! I'm Vishan Budhan, an Industrial and Systems Engineering student at Rutgers. I love meeting people and helping them find their place in engineering!

choices.label: What do you do outside class?

intro_sme.text: I'm also the Internal Vice President of the Society of Manufacturing Engineers, or SME. We help students connect, learn, and get involved beyond the classroom.

hook.text: Now, quick question: ever finished a long study session and realized your shoulders were basically touching your ears? Yeah, your desk might owe you an apology.

choices.label: I know exactly what you mean.
What does that have to do with engineering?

setup.text: This is our ergonomics and human-factors setup. We use equipment like this to study where people look and how they move while doing tasks.

eye_main.text: Eye tracking helps us study visual attention—where someone looks during a task. If an important control is hard to find, that can be a design problem, not a people problem.

choices.label: Can you give me an example?

body_main.text: We can also study posture and body movement. Lots of awkward reaching or twisting may be a sign that a workstation could be designed better.

ise_main.text: That's where ISE comes in! We look at how people, equipment, and workflows interact—and try to make the whole system safer, easier, and more effective.

choices.label: How do you know an improvement worked?

closing_setup.text: My favorite part is that the best solution isn't always a fancier machine. Sometimes it's moving a tool closer, making a display clearer, or simply listening to the person doing the work.

choices.label: How does SME connect to this?

sme.text: SME is a student community around manufacturing and engineering. For me, it's about helping students meet each other, share ideas, and find opportunities to get involved.

sme_join.text: Reaching out to an officer or coming to a student event is a good place to start. You don't need to know everything about manufacturing to be curious about it!

choices.label: What does being internal VP involve?

sme_role.text: As Internal Vice President, I help support the student organization's internal work and connections. I especially enjoy being someone people can come to with questions.

choices.label: How does it relate to ISE?

sme_connection.text: Manufacturing involves people as much as machines. SME gives students a way to learn from each other, and ergonomics reminds us to design work for the people doing it.

choices.label: Tell me more about the setup.

ergonomics.text: Ergonomics means fitting the task to the person—not asking the person to keep adapting to a badly designed task. Less awkward reaching is a pretty good start!

human_factors.text: Human factors looks at how people interact with tools, information, and environments. A system can work technically and still be confusing or uncomfortable to use.

choices.label: Can you give me a real example?

display_example.text: Imagine a crowded control screen. If the important warning is hard to notice, eye-tracking results might help engineers rethink where information appears.

choices.label: Okay, I can see why that matters.
Does eye tracking tell you what someone thinks?

eye_limits.text: Not exactly! It can show patterns of looking, but it doesn't directly tell us what someone's thinking. We'd combine it with observations and feedback.

feedback.text: We could ask someone what felt confusing or tiring, then compare that with what we observed. Data helps, but talking to the person matters too.

movement_data.text: An engineer might observe reach distance, repeated motions, or time spent in uncomfortable positions. You'd interpret that alongside the actual task and the person's feedback.

workstation_example.text: Think about picking up a tool over and over. Moving it closer or adjusting work height could reduce reaching without changing the entire process.

test_improvement.text: Absolutely. We'd compare the task before and after a change—maybe looking at reach, task time, comfort, or errors—then see whether it actually helped.

choices.label: That’s a useful way to think.

iteration.text: Then we'd try again! Engineering doesn't have to be a one-and-done thing. You listen, adjust, and test until the solution works for the people involved.

choices.label: Why does that matter in ISE?

finish.text: Thanks for hanging out! Remember, great engineering isn't just about what a system can do—it's about how well it works for people. Enjoy exploring, and check out SME if you're curious!

bye.text: No worries! Enjoy exploring the room, and feel free to come back if you have questions. I promise the ergonomics jokes don't get much worse.
